passages: Kairos Power just locked in a major construction partner with deep pockets.

Samsung C&T’s Engineering & Construction Group has committed up to $100 million to help build the Hermes 2 nuclear demonstration plant in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, a 50-megawatt reactor that represents the bleeding edge of advanced nuclear technology in the US.
Hermes 2 is the first project under a Master Plant Development Agreement that Kairos Power established with Google in 2024.
Kairos Power isn’t alone in chasing this market.
Companies like TerraPower (backed by Bill Gates), X-energy, and NuScale Power are all developing small modular reactors or advanced designs.
NuScale, which went public via a SPAC, faced a significant setback when its flagship project in Idaho was cancelled in 2023 due to rising costs.
For context, a typical US nuclear plant generates around 1,000 MW.
But the project is designed as a proof of concept that, if successful, Kairos Power can replicate across multiple sites to potentially reach that 500 MW target within a decade.

extraction.body: Kairos Power has picked engineering firm Samsung C&T to help build its 50-megawatt demonstration reactor for Google , which the nuclear startup is aiming to have completed by 2030. As part of the deal, Samsung C&T will make an equity investment in Kairos and provide “in-kind” engineering services, the combination of which is worth up to $100 million, Kairos Power said Monday. The equity investment will make up $70 million of the total, a Kairos spokesperson told TechCrunch. Samsung C&T has built or helped build about a dozen nuclear reactors around the globe. Kairos is part of a wave of nuclear startups that have benefited from the surge in power demand from AI data centers. Google first signed a deal with the company in fall 2024 , calling on Kairos to build nuclear reactors capable of generating about half a gigawatt of electricity by 2035. Currently, Kairos is building two reactors in Oak Ridge, Tennessee. The first, Hermes 1, is a low-power demonstrator that will help the company refine its commercial design. The second, Hermes 2, is Kairos’ first commercial-scale reactor. Output from Hermes will count as the first 50 megawatts of its deal with Google. The startup received approval from the Nuclear Regulatory Commission in late 2024 to build the reactors. It expects Hermes 2 to begin operating in 2030, in line with its original agreement with Google. Hermes 2 will be a fluoride salt-cooled high-temperature reactor, a design that has been floated for years but never built at commercial scale. Fluoride salts have high boiling points, which will help keep pressure levels low. That, in turn, will limit the risk of high-pressure blowouts in case of any parts failures. Kairos is also using a relatively new form of nuclear fuel known as TRISO, which encapsulates tiny seeds of uranium fuel in layers of ceramic and carbon, which are then loaded into billiard ball-sized spheres. The arrangement is intended to prevent meltdowns. The startup has about five years to get its first power plant up and running, which is an accelerated but manageable timeline in the nuclear industry. To fulfill the terms of its deal with Google, Kairos will need to move even faster on subsequent reactors, something Samsung C&T might be able to help with. "We're not asking for your trust," Torkan said, acknowledging some of Bungie's recent struggles.

"We know we have to earn it, and to do that, we need our games to deliver in ways that exceed your expectations of what you've come to love about the games that we make – and that starts with Destiny.
"Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it.
The five-minute upload features Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and head of product, GM of Marathon Josh Deane.

The two executives start their surprise talk with fans, promising that Sony has not completely abandoned the Destiny brand after months of fans pleading to see them either return to Destiny 2 or eventually create Destiny 3.

extraction.body: Bungie has said it is "absolutely not done with Destiny" just months after the controversial decision to end ongoing support for Destiny 2 . The five-minute upload features Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and head of product, GM of Marathon Josh Deane. The two executives start their surprise talk with fans, promising that Sony has not completely abandoned the Destiny brand after months of fans pleading to see them either return to Destiny 2 or eventually create Destiny 3. "We're not asking for your trust," Torkan said, acknowledging some of Bungie's recent struggles. "We know we have to earn it, and to do that, we need our games to deliver in ways that exceed your expectations of what you've come to love about the games that we make – and that starts with Destiny. "Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it. It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny. We have more stories to tell, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe." Deane clarified that Bungie's goal is to "return Destiny to its original promise." That means going back to "awe-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds." It's been a painful few months for the players who stuck by Destiny and Destiny 2 before substantial support came to an end with the Monument of Triumph update in June. Unfortunately, restoring that community and rebuilding trust will take even more time. "I wish we could just flip a freaking switch, but we're going to commit to unvaulting the Destiny 2 campaigns, the destinations, the raids that never should have been ripped away to begin with," Deane added. "They were an essential part of our journey together and definitely a place where we built memories with y'all." Bungie shared additional details with a post on its website . In a segment titled "Destiny Is Foundational to Our Future," the team excplitly called attention to the players who rallied together to give Destiny another shot at life . Through all of the uncertainty, comments , and livestream chat takeovers , it seems those in charge heard fans loud and clear. "Your voices mattered, and the way you showed up made a real impact," the message said. "You reminded everyone how much this world, its history, and its future still mean to you." As teased in the video, the first step to a future with more Destiny stories means unvaulting experiences that were previously locked away. The studio acknowledged that the vaulting certain experiences "had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny," adding that "Destiny 2 is more than just the content itself." "It is a place where players have built memories together, formed lasting friendships, and shared experiences that have stayed with them for years. We cannot change the decision we made, but we can acknowledge its impact and do the work to make it right by restoring these important parts of Destiny’s history." Bungie said it is just getting started on the work required to unvault campaigns, destinations, and raids. All of this content will be made available for "all Destiny 2 players," though the developers caution that "bringing back this content is not as simple as restoring old files." Changes made post-Beyond Light will require the studio to update lighting, encounters, combatants, and more. It's work that will take time, but the fact the effort is being put in at all is something that will no doubt have fans waiting on the edges of their seats, no matter how long it takes. "When we look to the future of Destiny all up this restoration is the first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve," the message continued. "We’ll have more details on our unvaulting efforts in the coming months, and we’re very excited to share more about our vision to celebrate Destiny’s legacy and build its future with you all as soon as we can." So, what exactly does this mean? While fans may not want to get their hopes up that this video serves as confirmation of Destiny 3 quite yet, Deane did say the plan is to deliver "new Destiny stories and games" that players deserve. In other words, the promise of more Destiny, a day many thought may never come, is here. Aside from the untimely demise of the now-revived Destiny 2, Bungie itself has undergone a wave of significant changes in recent months. In June, the company was confirmed to have been impacted by layoffs affecting almost 300 staff . A few weeks ago, the company confirmed plans to sublease parts of its Bellevue, Washington headquarters . Will Destiny 2 relaunch with a new name? Will we ever get Destiny 3? Will Bungie get to breathe life into its reported Destiny Infinity idea ? Only time will tell, but one thing is certain: Marathon will not be replacing Destiny . sources.title: Bungie says it’s ‘not done with Destiny’ and will bring back vaulted content
passages: Months after seemingly giving up on Destiny 2, Bungie now says it’s planning to restore vaulted content in the game like campaigns, destinations, and raids.
The decision reverses the Destiny Content Vault that Bungie created six years ago, controversially removing older content from Destiny 2 that players had paid to access.
“We understand that removing these experiences had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny,” admits Bungie.
Bungie is only committing to building a “stronger long-term future for Destiny” right now.
The changes are a little vague right now, but it sounds like Marathon really needs to change and attract more players if it’s to be a sustainable project for Bungie.
There’s no mention of such a project, despite fans desperately pleading for a successor to Destiny 2 in multiple high-profile Twitch streams in recent weeks.

extraction.body: Months after seemingly giving up on Destiny 2, Bungie now says it’s planning to restore vaulted content in the game like campaigns, destinations, and raids. The decision reverses the Destiny Content Vault that Bungie created six years ago, controversially removing older content from Destiny 2 that players had paid to access. “We understand that removing these experiences had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny,” admits Bungie. “We cannot change the decision we made, but we can acknowledge its impact and do the work to make it right by restoring these important parts of Destiny’s history.“ All Destiny 2 players will get access to the vaulted content, but it’s not a simple switch of a button for Bungie. The developer made big changes to Destiny 2 with the Beyond Light expansion, meaning it has to go back and update lighting, encounters, combatants, and other underlying systems for this older content. The mod lets players access older areas in Destiny 2 that had been vaulted, but not the exact campaigns and missions that players had experienced previously. Bungie now says its own restoration project is the “first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve.” Could that be a Destiny 3 sequel? There’s no mention of such a project, despite fans desperately pleading for a successor to Destiny 2 in multiple high-profile Twitch streams in recent weeks. Bungie is only committing to building a “stronger long-term future for Destiny” right now. Alongside the Destiny 2 efforts, Bungie is also admitting that Marathon, its extraction shooter, didn’t “reach as many players as we had hoped, and we also know and understand that the game needs to evolve.” That means Marathon will expand deeper into a survival experience. The changes are a little vague right now, but it sounds like Marathon really needs to change and attract more players if it’s to be a sustainable project for Bungie.

extraction.body: Bungie has said it is "absolutely not done with Destiny" just months after the controversial decision to end ongoing support for Destiny 2 . The five-minute upload features Bungie studio head Poria Torkan and head of product, GM of Marathon Josh Deane. The two executives start their surprise talk with fans, promising that Sony has not completely abandoned the Destiny brand after months of fans pleading to see them either return to Destiny 2 or eventually create Destiny 3. "We're not asking for your trust," Torkan said, acknowledging some of Bungie's recent struggles. "We know we have to earn it, and to do that, we need our games to deliver in ways that exceed your expectations of what you've come to love about the games that we make – and that starts with Destiny. "Bungie wouldn't be what it is today without it. It's the foundation upon which everything else rests, and we are absolutely not done with Destiny. We have more stories to tell, but we have to do it right and give our teams the time they need to do justice to this amazing universe." Deane clarified that Bungie's goal is to "return Destiny to its original promise." That means going back to "awe-inspiring mystery, the sense of discovery, and the promise of a community of Guardians rallying together, raging against impossible odds." It's been a painful few months for the players who stuck by Destiny and Destiny 2 before substantial support came to an end with the Monument of Triumph update in June. Unfortunately, restoring that community and rebuilding trust will take even more time. "I wish we could just flip a freaking switch, but we're going to commit to unvaulting the Destiny 2 campaigns, the destinations, the raids that never should have been ripped away to begin with," Deane added. "They were an essential part of our journey together and definitely a place where we built memories with y'all." Bungie shared additional details with a post on its website . In a segment titled "Destiny Is Foundational to Our Future," the team excplitly called attention to the players who rallied together to give Destiny another shot at life . Through all of the uncertainty, comments , and livestream chat takeovers , it seems those in charge heard fans loud and clear. "Your voices mattered, and the way you showed up made a real impact," the message said. "You reminded everyone how much this world, its history, and its future still mean to you." As teased in the video, the first step to a future with more Destiny stories means unvaulting experiences that were previously locked away. The studio acknowledged that the vaulting certain experiences "had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny," adding that "Destiny 2 is more than just the content itself." "It is a place where players have built memories together, formed lasting friendships, and shared experiences that have stayed with them for years. We cannot change the decision we made, but we can acknowledge its impact and do the work to make it right by restoring these important parts of Destiny’s history." Bungie said it is just getting started on the work required to unvault campaigns, destinations, and raids. All of this content will be made available for "all Destiny 2 players," though the developers caution that "bringing back this content is not as simple as restoring old files." Changes made post-Beyond Light will require the studio to update lighting, encounters, combatants, and more. It's work that will take time, but the fact the effort is being put in at all is something that will no doubt have fans waiting on the edges of their seats, no matter how long it takes. "When we look to the future of Destiny all up this restoration is the first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve," the message continued. "We’ll have more details on our unvaulting efforts in the coming months, and we’re very excited to share more about our vision to celebrate Destiny’s legacy and build its future with you all as soon as we can." So, what exactly does this mean? While fans may not want to get their hopes up that this video serves as confirmation of Destiny 3 quite yet, Deane did say the plan is to deliver "new Destiny stories and games" that players deserve. In other words, the promise of more Destiny, a day many thought may never come, is here. Aside from the untimely demise of the now-revived Destiny 2, Bungie itself has undergone a wave of significant changes in recent months. In June, the company was confirmed to have been impacted by layoffs affecting almost 300 staff . A few weeks ago, the company confirmed plans to sublease parts of its Bellevue, Washington headquarters . Will Destiny 2 relaunch with a new name? Will we ever get Destiny 3? Will Bungie get to breathe life into its reported Destiny Infinity idea ? Only time will tell, but one thing is certain: Marathon will not be replacing Destiny . sources.title: Bungie says it’s ‘not done with Destiny’ and will bring back vaulted content
passages: Months after seemingly giving up on Destiny 2, Bungie now says it’s planning to restore vaulted content in the game like campaigns, destinations, and raids.
The decision reverses the Destiny Content Vault that Bungie created six years ago, controversially removing older content from Destiny 2 that players had paid to access.
“We understand that removing these experiences had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny,” admits Bungie.
Bungie is only committing to building a “stronger long-term future for Destiny” right now.
The changes are a little vague right now, but it sounds like Marathon really needs to change and attract more players if it’s to be a sustainable project for Bungie.
There’s no mention of such a project, despite fans desperately pleading for a successor to Destiny 2 in multiple high-profile Twitch streams in recent weeks.

extraction.body: Months after seemingly giving up on Destiny 2, Bungie now says it’s planning to restore vaulted content in the game like campaigns, destinations, and raids. The decision reverses the Destiny Content Vault that Bungie created six years ago, controversially removing older content from Destiny 2 that players had paid to access. “We understand that removing these experiences had a lasting impact on player trust and enjoyment of Destiny,” admits Bungie. “We cannot change the decision we made, but we can acknowledge its impact and do the work to make it right by restoring these important parts of Destiny’s history.“ All Destiny 2 players will get access to the vaulted content, but it’s not a simple switch of a button for Bungie. The developer made big changes to Destiny 2 with the Beyond Light expansion, meaning it has to go back and update lighting, encounters, combatants, and other underlying systems for this older content. The mod lets players access older areas in Destiny 2 that had been vaulted, but not the exact campaigns and missions that players had experienced previously. Bungie now says its own restoration project is the “first step to lay the foundation for how we reforge into new stories and games that you all deserve.” Could that be a Destiny 3 sequel? There’s no mention of such a project, despite fans desperately pleading for a successor to Destiny 2 in multiple high-profile Twitch streams in recent weeks. Bungie is only committing to building a “stronger long-term future for Destiny” right now. Alongside the Destiny 2 efforts, Bungie is also admitting that Marathon, its extraction shooter, didn’t “reach as many players as we had hoped, and we also know and understand that the game needs to evolve.” That means Marathon will expand deeper into a survival experience. The changes are a little vague right now, but it sounds like Marathon really needs to change and attract more players if it’s to be a sustainable project for Bungie.

extraction.body: Priority Technology Holdings, Inc. Announces Definitive Agreement with Investor Group Led by Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore to Take Company Private Priority Stockholders to Receive $8.05/Share in Cash, a 65% Premium to Unaffected Share Price Transaction Unanimously Recommended by Special Committee of Priority’s Independent and Disinterested Directors and Approved by the Board of Directors ALPHARETTA, Ga.--( BUSINESS WIRE )-- Priority Technology Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: PRTH) (“Priority” or the “Company”), the payments and banking solutions provider that streamlines collecting, storing, lending and sending money to unlock revenue opportunities, today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement (the “Agreement”) with an investor group led by Thomas Priore, the Company’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (the “Investor Group”), pursuant to which the Investor Group will acquire all outstanding shares of Priority’s common stock that it does not already own for $8.05 per share in cash. The all-cash transaction represents an enterprise value of approximately $1.6 billion. The transaction delivers a 65% premium to the Company’s closing share price on November 7, 2025, the last trading day before public disclosure of the Investor Group’s preliminary, non-binding proposal (the “Initial Proposal”) to acquire the remaining shares of the Company’s common stock that the Investor Group does not currently hold. The transaction represents a 38% premium to the Company’s closing share price on September 18, 2026, the last trading day prior to the announcement of the definitive agreement. The transaction was unanimously recommended by a special committee of independent and disinterested directors (the “Special Committee”), which conducted a robust review process with the assistance of its independent legal and financial advisors. Michael Passilla, Chair of the Special Committee, said: “After a comprehensive evaluation of the proposal, a rigorous valuation analysis, and extensive negotiations with Tom and his affiliates, we are delivering a transaction that provides compelling and certain value to Priority’s unaffiliated stockholders. We believe this is the best path for the unaffiliated stockholders to realize the significant value from their investment in the Company.” Thomas Priore, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Priority, said: “I am pleased to have reached an agreement that delivers meaningful value to our stockholders and positions the Company to achieve our vision for Connected Commerce. I am deeply proud of what our team has built, and I am excited to lead the Company into this promising next chapter.” Independent Review and Valuation Process As previously announced, the Special Committee was established by the Company’s Board of Directors to evaluate the Investor Group’s Initial Proposal. Following a rigorous valuation analysis and comprehensive review of the Initial Proposal, the Special Committee engaged in extensive negotiations with the Investor Group, including with Mr. Priore, who had informed the Special Committee that he does not intend to sell his stake in the Company to any third party, as disclosed in the Schedule 13D filed in December 2025. The negotiations resulted in improved transaction terms, including a more than 30% price increase, for the benefit of Priority’s unaffiliated stockholders. The Board of Directors, having received the unanimous recommendation of the Special Committee, determined that the proposed transaction is in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders. The Board recommends that Priority stockholders vote in favor of the proposed transaction at a special meeting of shareholders that will be held to vote on the transaction. Transaction Details and Approvals Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in the Agreement, holders of the Company’s common stock (other than shares held by the Investor Group) will receive $8.05 per share in cash at the closing of the transaction. The transaction is being financed, in part, by equity commitments from funds advised by Searchlight Capital Partners, L.P. (“Searchlight”), and is not subject to any financing conditions. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals and approval by the holders of a majority of Priority’s common stock that are not affiliated with the Investor Group. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Upon completion of the transaction, the Company will be a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Additional information regarding the transaction will be filed by Priority with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) in a Current Report on Form 8-K. The Company also plans to file a proxy statement and a Rule 13e-3 transaction statement with the SEC in connection with the solicitation of proxies from stockholders to vote in favor of the adoption of the Agreement. Advisors Barclays is serving as exclusive financial advisor to the Special Committee. Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP is serving as legal counsel to the Special Committee. TD Securities is serving as exclusive placement agent to the Investor Group. McDermott Will & Schulte LLP is serving as legal counsel to the Investor Group. Nixon Peabody LLP is serving as legal counsel to the Company. Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to Searchlight. About Searchlight Searchlight is a global private investment firm with $17 billion in assets under management and offices in London, New York, Miami and Toronto. Founded on the principle that creative, engaged ownership creates superior outcomes, Searchlight partners with management teams to build market-leading businesses across its core sectors of telecommunications, media, business, industrial and financial services. Searchlight seeks to invest in businesses where its flexible approach and strategic support accelerate value creation for all stakeholders, leveraging deep sector expertise and a global network to help portfolio companies realize their full potential. Under the definitive agreement, the investor group will purchase all outstanding shares it does not already own for $8.05 per share in cash.

The definitive take-private agreement establishes a specific cash consideration for unaffiliated Priority shareholders, shifting the investment focus from the company's operating performance towards the likelihood and timing of transaction completion.

Investors will also be watching for the scheduling and outcome of the special shareholder meeting, where approval from a majority of shares held by investors unaffiliated with the acquiring group will be required.
The involvement of Priore, who already holds a stake in Priority, also makes the transaction's governance structure relevant.

Priority Technology Holdings has agreed to an all-cash acquisition led by its chairman and CEO, offering shareholders a 38% premium to the latest closing price ahead of the announcement. Priority Technology Holdings (NASDAQ:PRTH) has entered into a definitive take-private agreement valued at approximately $1.6 billion. Unaffiliated shareholders will receive $8.05 per share in cash, representing a 38% premium to the September 18 closing price. The acquisition price increased by more than 30% following negotiations with an independent special committee. The transaction has no financing condition but requires regulatory clearance and approval from a majority of unaffiliated shareholders. Completion is expected in the first half of 2027, after which Priority shares will be delisted from Nasdaq. Priority Technology Holdings has agreed to be acquired by an investor group led by Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore in a transaction that would end the payments and banking technology company's public listing. Under the definitive agreement, the investor group will purchase all outstanding shares it does not already own for $8.05 per share in cash. The offer represents a 65% premium to Priority's closing share price on November 7, 2025, before the initial acquisition proposal became public, and a 38% premium to its September 18, 2026 closing price. The $1.6 billion enterprise-value transaction follows negotiations between the investor group and a special committee of independent directors. The committee secured a price increase of more than 30% from the initial proposal before unanimously recommending the agreement. Priority's board subsequently approved the transaction. Financing will include equity commitments from funds advised by Searchlight Capital Partners. The agreement is not subject to financing conditions. The definitive take-private agreement establishes a specific cash consideration for unaffiliated Priority shareholders, shifting the investment focus from the company's operating performance towards the likelihood and timing of transaction completion. The $8.05 acquisition price provides a reference point for evaluating the stock while the deal remains pending. However, the consideration is payable only upon closing, and the agreement remains subject to several conditions. The involvement of Priore, who already holds a stake in Priority, also makes the transaction's governance structure relevant. The independent special committee negotiated the terms after Priore disclosed that he did not intend to sell his stake to a third party. The committee's involvement and the requirement for approval from unaffiliated shareholders are therefore important elements of the transaction. Although the absence of a financing condition removes one potential obstacle, regulatory approvals and the shareholder vote remain outstanding. For investors, the central uncertainty is whether the agreed transaction will close on the proposed terms and within the expected timeframe. If completed, Priority will become privately held, eliminating its Nasdaq listing and ending public-market participation for shareholders receiving the cash consideration. Priority expects the acquisition to close during the first half of 2027, with several developments still to come. The company plans to file a proxy statement and a Rule 13e-3 transaction statement with the Securities and Exchange Commission, providing additional information about the transaction and shareholder approval process. Investors will also be watching for the scheduling and outcome of the special shareholder meeting, where approval from a majority of shares held by investors unaffiliated with the acquiring group will be required. Regulatory clearance and confirmation of the closing date will determine when eligible shareholders can receive the $8.05 cash consideration.

extraction.body: Priority Technology Holdings, Inc. Announces Definitive Agreement with Investor Group Led by Chairman and CEO Thomas Priore to Take Company Private Priority Stockholders to Receive $8.05/Share in Cash, a 65% Premium to Unaffected Share Price Transaction Unanimously Recommended by Special Committee of Priority’s Independent and Disinterested Directors and Approved by the Board of Directors ALPHARETTA, Ga.--( BUSINESS WIRE )-- Priority Technology Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: PRTH) (“Priority” or the “Company”), the payments and banking solutions provider that streamlines collecting, storing, lending and sending money to unlock revenue opportunities, today announced it has entered into a definitive agreement (the “Agreement”) with an investor group led by Thomas Priore, the Company’s Chairman and Chief Executive Officer (the “Investor Group”), pursuant to which the Investor Group will acquire all outstanding shares of Priority’s common stock that it does not already own for $8.05 per share in cash. The all-cash transaction represents an enterprise value of approximately $1.6 billion. The transaction delivers a 65% premium to the Company’s closing share price on November 7, 2025, the last trading day before public disclosure of the Investor Group’s preliminary, non-binding proposal (the “Initial Proposal”) to acquire the remaining shares of the Company’s common stock that the Investor Group does not currently hold. The transaction represents a 38% premium to the Company’s closing share price on September 18, 2026, the last trading day prior to the announcement of the definitive agreement. The transaction was unanimously recommended by a special committee of independent and disinterested directors (the “Special Committee”), which conducted a robust review process with the assistance of its independent legal and financial advisors. Michael Passilla, Chair of the Special Committee, said: “After a comprehensive evaluation of the proposal, a rigorous valuation analysis, and extensive negotiations with Tom and his affiliates, we are delivering a transaction that provides compelling and certain value to Priority’s unaffiliated stockholders. We believe this is the best path for the unaffiliated stockholders to realize the significant value from their investment in the Company.” Thomas Priore, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Priority, said: “I am pleased to have reached an agreement that delivers meaningful value to our stockholders and positions the Company to achieve our vision for Connected Commerce. I am deeply proud of what our team has built, and I am excited to lead the Company into this promising next chapter.” Independent Review and Valuation Process As previously announced, the Special Committee was established by the Company’s Board of Directors to evaluate the Investor Group’s Initial Proposal. Following a rigorous valuation analysis and comprehensive review of the Initial Proposal, the Special Committee engaged in extensive negotiations with the Investor Group, including with Mr. Priore, who had informed the Special Committee that he does not intend to sell his stake in the Company to any third party, as disclosed in the Schedule 13D filed in December 2025. The negotiations resulted in improved transaction terms, including a more than 30% price increase, for the benefit of Priority’s unaffiliated stockholders. The Board of Directors, having received the unanimous recommendation of the Special Committee, determined that the proposed transaction is in the best interests of the Company and its stockholders. The Board recommends that Priority stockholders vote in favor of the proposed transaction at a special meeting of shareholders that will be held to vote on the transaction. Transaction Details and Approvals Subject to the satisfaction of the conditions set forth in the Agreement, holders of the Company’s common stock (other than shares held by the Investor Group) will receive $8.05 per share in cash at the closing of the transaction. The transaction is being financed, in part, by equity commitments from funds advised by Searchlight Capital Partners, L.P. (“Searchlight”), and is not subject to any financing conditions. The transaction is subject to customary closing conditions, including regulatory approvals and approval by the holders of a majority of Priority’s common stock that are not affiliated with the Investor Group. The transaction is expected to close in the first half of 2027. Upon completion of the transaction, the Company will be a privately held company, and its common stock will no longer be listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market. Additional information regarding the transaction will be filed by Priority with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC”) in a Current Report on Form 8-K. The Company also plans to file a proxy statement and a Rule 13e-3 transaction statement with the SEC in connection with the solicitation of proxies from stockholders to vote in favor of the adoption of the Agreement. Advisors Barclays is serving as exclusive financial advisor to the Special Committee. Paul, Weiss, Rifkind, Wharton & Garrison LLP is serving as legal counsel to the Special Committee. TD Securities is serving as exclusive placement agent to the Investor Group. McDermott Will & Schulte LLP is serving as legal counsel to the Investor Group. Nixon Peabody LLP is serving as legal counsel to the Company. Latham & Watkins LLP is serving as legal counsel to Searchlight. About Searchlight Searchlight is a global private investment firm with $17 billion in assets under management and offices in London, New York, Miami and Toronto. Founded on the principle that creative, engaged ownership creates superior outcomes, Searchlight partners with management teams to build market-leading businesses across its core sectors of telecommunications, media, business, industrial and financial services. Searchlight seeks to invest in businesses where its flexible approach and strategic support accelerate value creation for all stakeholders, leveraging deep sector expertise and a global network to help portfolio companies realize their full potential. For more information, please visit www.searchlightcap.com . sources.title: Why Is Crypto Up Today? Oil Prices Drop, Short Sellers Squeezed, and Bitcoin Reclaims Key Level After 45 Weeks - finance.yahoo.com
passages: The crypto market is currently rallying, fueled by a fourth straight day of lower oil prices, which helped push the 10-year yield below 5%.
Bitcoin also closed the week above a key level it hadn't held for 45 weeks, and about $648 million in short positions were forced to close.
While the first two factors can have lasting effects, the third is a one-time event, and recent ETF activity added only $6.21 million for the week ending September 19.
The answer lies in three main factors that developed between September 18 and September 21: a drop in oil prices, a strong weekly close for Bitcoin, and a surge in short sellers.
Bitcoin's first weekly close above the 50-week moving average in 45 weeks triggered a $300 million short squeeze, lifting MSTR 7%.
Funding rates for XRP perpetual contracts, which ensure futures prices stay aligned with cash prices, had been negative for over a week, meaning short sellers were compensating long holders.
Once the price began to rise, these shorts faced the most pressure, contributing to XRP's 6.4% gain compared to Bitcoin's 5.3%.
Exchanges liquidated approximately $262.30 million in shorts within an hour as Bitcoin passed this level, according to CoinGlass.
Of that total, about $218.55 million came from Bitcoin shorts, with just $9.53 million coming from long positions.
Alex Thorn from Galaxy has noted that Bitcoin has reclaimed this average 13 times since 2011, and in 11 out of 13 instances, it did not drop to new lows afterward.
ETF inflows of just $6 million and failed crypto legislation mean the rally rests entirely on Bitcoin clearing $85,000 and oil staying soft.
Bitcoin last closed above this line on November 9, 2025, and has spent 44 weeks below it since.

ANN ARBOR, Mich., Sept. 15, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Merge today launched MergeIQ™, an artificial intelligence layer that embeds practical intelligence applications across the Merge platform. MergeIQ provides a scalable foundation for applying AI across radiology, cardiology, pathology and other imaging specialties. The first MergeIQ applications, RelevancyIQ™ and NaviIQ, are available within Merge Workflow Orchestrator. Embedded directly into the radiologist's diagnostic reading workflow, they provide relevant prior information and clinical context keeping radiologists in their current workflow, while bringing supporting data directly to the point of interpretation. RelevancyIQ: Identifies and ranks prior reports according to their relevance to the current case, helping radiologists focus on the historical context most likely to inform interpretation. NaviIQ : Searches within prior reports to surface relevant findings and historical context that may inform interpretation of the current study. Together, these applications are designed to streamline access to relevant prior information at a moment when imaging volumes continue to rise and reports span more modalities than ever. Data from the American Medical Association show radiologists fifth on its list (45.2%) for burnout rates among medical specialties. RelevancyIQ and NaviIQ are designed to locate relevant prior information and bring useful data directly into the existing diagnostic reading workflow. As imaging volumes increase and findings span multiple modalities, this integrated approach helps radiologists remain focused on interpretation rather than searching across disconnected systems. At the platform level, MergeIQ provides a governed, scalable approach to AI adoption within an established enterprise imaging environment. It combines fine-tuned foundation models, third-party models and AI models developed in-house, then embeds the resulting intelligence within existing applications and workflows. Applied within the imaging context, these capabilities search large volumes of prior reports to surface information prioritized by relevancy to the current exam. Imaging-specific data, integrations and workflow controls support their practical clinical use. This approach enables organizations to advance innovation without adding another standalone platform or increasing the number of systems IT teams must manage. It extends the value of prior investments while allowing organizations to adopt new capabilities with less disruption and at a pace aligned with their priorities. "MergeIQ represents a comprehensive approach to AI across the Merge platform, one that begins with the clinical and operational challenges imaging organizations need to address and applies technology in a practical, responsible and scalable manner," said Ashish Sant, General Manager, Merge. "RelevancyIQ and NaviIQ bring relevant clinical context directly into the radiologist's diagnostic reading workflow, delivering value today while establishing a foundation for additional AI applications across Merge solutions." MergeIQ launches first within Merge Workflow Orchestrator, which unifies enterprise worklists to support caseload management, interpretation and collaboration. Over time, Merge plans to expand MergeIQ across the platform, bringing practical intelligence to additional applications and imaging specialties. About Merge Merge empowers healthcare organizations with advanced medical imaging solutions to deliver reliable imaging, less complexity, and better care. Merge is trusted by 6 of the 10 largest U.S. health systems. Merge Imaging Suite, built on a cloud-native foundation, provides capabilities for Vendor-Neutral Archive (VNA) for secure, enterprise-wide data management; Enterprise Diagnostic Viewing for anytime, anywhere image access; and Workflow Orchestration to streamline imaging workflows. Merge's portfolio also includes PACS for multi-specialty support and advanced mammography capabilities, Cardiology solutions for improved hemodynamics workflows and comprehensive CVIS support, and support for Digital Pathology.
